structuralContract.indexRule: Every indexed term points to one unique concept teaching unit.
structuralContract.analogyRule: Every analogy is adjacent to an explicit limit.
structuralContract.workedCase: A client handover email from meeting notes and the current service policy.
structuralContract.releaseBoundary: Independent accuracy and unfamiliar-reader review are required before local admission; deployment and publication require separate authority.

conceptEvidenceGroups.boundary: Formal system and glossary sources support the core distinctions; the surrounding product map and examples are explicitly LAiDIES synthesis.
Architectures, tokenizers, training methods and sampling controls vary by model and product; hardware claims are bounded to the cited general mechanism.
Prompt/context terms are durable; session, memory, context limits and cutoffs are product/model-specific and require before-release recheck.
Implementations vary. Retrieval, grounding, permission, containment and validation are intentionally separated; none alone proves truth.
Agent terminology varies. Harness, skill and loop engineering are explicitly scoped as LAiDIES product-engineering vocabulary rather than universal standards.
Evaluation evidence applies only to defined tasks and conditions; live consequential claims still require claim-specific verification.
Reasoning-model and AGI labels are not universal; AI-winter causation is not claimed; access labels do not establish safety or accuracy.

claimClusters.claim: The model is one trained component inside a wider product and AI system.
claimClusters.limitation: The surrounding product map is LAiDIES instructional synthesis; implementations vary.

claimClusters.claim: Training adjusts parameters before the current task; inference applies the trained model to new input.
claimClusters.limitation: Training methods and model architectures vary.

claimClusters.claim: Current context, session state, product memory and training-time knowledge are distinct.
claimClusters.limitation: Session and memory behaviour are product-specific and must be rechecked before release.

claimClusters.claim: Retrieval, grounding, permissions and containment solve different problems.
Agents and harnesses surround models with tools, state, routing and controls; MCP standardizes a connection, not trust or permission.
claimClusters.limitation: Agent terminology is not standardized across the field.

claimClusters.claim: Plausible generation is not evidence; consequential claims require verification outside the generated answer.
claimClusters.limitation: Verification methods depend on the claim and consequence.

claimClusters.claim: AGI and access labels require their exact definition, test and terms rather than assumptions from the label.
claimClusters.limitation: AGI definitions remain disputed; access terms must be checked for each system.
